name: Alabama
climateOverview: Humid subtropical climate with sharp winter frost and sudden damp cold snaps that trigger heavy heating loads after long periods of inactivity.
commonFurnaceIssues: Corroded ignition contacts from humid off-seasons, failed heat pump reversing valves, and clogged furnace drain traps.
licensingBody: State of Alabama Board of Heating, Air Conditioning & Refrigeration Contractors

name: Alaska
climateOverview: Extreme subarctic winter conditions with sustained sub-zero temperatures, intense wind chills, and continuous round-the-clock heating reliance.
commonFurnaceIssues: Frozen condensate drainage lines in 90%+ AFUE condensing units, draft inducer motor burnout, and cracked primary heat exchangers.
licensingBody: Alaska Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing

name: Arizona
climateOverview: Desert winter climate with intense daytime-to-nighttime temperature swings of 30°F+ causing rapid daily heating ignition cycles.
commonFurnaceIssues: Fine desert dust coating flame sensors and burners during months of summer AC use, resulting in startup ignition lockouts.
licensingBody: Arizona Registrar of Contractors

name: Arkansas
climateOverview: Four-season climate featuring sudden ice storms and damp Ozark winter cold fronts that demand immediate, reliable furnace response.
commonFurnaceIssues: Thermocouple degradation, faulty limit switches from restricted filter airflow, and gas valve pressure irregularities.
licensingBody: Arkansas Department of Labor and Licensing (HVACR Division)

name: California
climateOverview: Diverse regional climate ranging from damp coastal marine chills to Sierra snowstorms and Central Valley valley-fog cold snaps.
commonFurnaceIssues: Ultra-low NOx burner failure, older atmospheric draft chimney issues in mid-century homes, and electronic control board faults.
licensingBody: California Contractors State License Board (CSLB C-20)

name: Colorado
climateOverview: High-altitude Rocky Mountain winter with heavy snowfall, sub-zero cold waves, and thin air requiring precise combustion air adjustment.
commonFurnaceIssues: High-altitude pressure switch calibration issues, restricted combustion intake vents due to snow drifts, and blower motor strain.
licensingBody: Colorado Department of Regulatory Agencies (DORA)

name: Connecticut
climateOverview: New England coastal and inland winter cold with heavy nor'easters, freezing rain, and sustained below-freezing temperatures.
commonFurnaceIssues: Cracked heat exchangers in older housing stock, oil-to-gas converted burner issues, and failed draft inducer blowers.
licensingBody: Connecticut Department of Consumer Protection (Occupational Licensing)

name: Delaware
climateOverview: Mid-Atlantic coastal humidity mixed with freezing winter winds off Delaware Bay and the Atlantic Ocean.
commonFurnaceIssues: Salt air corrosion on exterior intake terminals, clogged condensate traps, and faulty ignition control modules.
licensingBody: Delaware Division of Professional Regulation

name: Florida
climateOverview: Primarily mild winters punctuated by sharp northern panhandle and central freezes that catch unmaintained heating systems unprepared.
commonFurnaceIssues: Dust burning odors on first winter startup, auxiliary strip heat failure, and corroded electrical sequencers.
licensingBody: Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation (DBPR)

name: Georgia
climateOverview: Piedmont and Appalachian winter chills with periodic severe ice storms and rapid 24-hour temperature plunges.
commonFurnaceIssues: Dirty flame sensors causing burner drop-out within seconds, dual-fuel heat pump defrost board failures, and clogged air filters.
licensingBody: Georgia State Licensing Board for Conditioned Air Contractors

name: Hawaii
climateOverview: Tropical climate with targeted high-elevation heating needs on Maui (Upcountry) and the Big Island where overnight temperatures drop into the 40s.
commonFurnaceIssues: High salt humidity corrosion on electrical contacts and gas supply lines in high-altitude volcanic residential zones.
licensingBody: Hawaii Professional and Vocational Licensing Division

name: Idaho
climateOverview: Intermountain Northwest cold with prolonged sub-freezing winters, heavy mountain snow, and dry freezing inversion layers.
commonFurnaceIssues: Flue pipe freeze-ups, cracked heat exchangers from heavy continuous run-times, and blower capacitor degradation.
licensingBody: Idaho Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses (DOPL)

name: Illinois
climateOverview: Severe Midwestern continental winters with lake-effect blizzards, Arctic polar vortex events, and sub-zero wind chills for weeks.
commonFurnaceIssues: Pressure switch lockouts from iced vent terminations, cracked cast-iron and tubular heat exchangers, and continuous limit switch trips.
licensingBody: Illinois Department of Public Health & Local Municipal Licensing Boards

name: Indiana
climateOverview: Classic Ohio Valley winters featuring heavy snowfall, sleet, and harsh freezing conditions requiring 24/7 heating dependability.
commonFurnaceIssues: Worn hot surface igniters (HSI), draft inducer motor bearing failure, and blower run capacitor burnouts.
licensingBody: Indiana Professional Licensing Agency

name: Iowa
climateOverview: Open plains winter with relentless arctic winds, sub-zero overnight temperatures, and heavy snow drifts blocking sidewall vents.
commonFurnaceIssues: Frozen exterior PVC exhaust pipes, combustion air starvation, and high-limit thermal switch failures.
licensingBody: Iowa Plumbing and Mechanical Systems Board

name: Kansas
climateOverview: Great Plains weather extremes with sharp polar fronts, sudden blizzards, and fierce winter wind chills.
commonFurnaceIssues: Ignition module failure, dirty burner orifices restricting flame spread, and return duct static pressure restrictions.
licensingBody: Kansas Board of Technical Professions & Local County Jurisdictions

name: Kentucky
climateOverview: Humid continental climate with frequent freezing rain, sudden freeze-thaw cycles, and damp winter cold.

name: Louisiana
climateOverview: Humid Gulf Coast climate where sudden arctic cold fronts clash with humid air, creating bone-chilling damp cold snaps.

name: Maine
climateOverview: Harsh maritime and northern forest winters with prolonged deep freezes, heavy coastal nor'easters, and multi-foot snow accumulations.

name: Maryland
climateOverview: Mid-Atlantic winter weather with damp Chesapeake Bay winds, icy precipitation, and freeze-thaw cycles stressing mechanical systems.

name: Massachusetts
climateOverview: Intense New England winter with historic blizzard events, coastal gales, and deep sustained freezes testing aging heating infrastructure.

name: Missouri

name: Montana
climateOverview: High northern plains and alpine winter characterized by severe sub-zero cold spells and heavy mountain snowfall.

name: Nebraska
climateOverview: Intense winter prairie winds, deep drifting snow, and sustained freezing temperatures throughout December through March.

name: Nevada
climateOverview: High desert and mountain climates with freezing nighttime lows in Las Vegas and heavy Sierra snowfall in Reno/Sparks.

name: New Hampshire

climateOverview: Extreme continental northern climate with prolonged -30°F wind chills and blizzard conditions where heating outages are hazardous.

name: Ohio
